column8: Wed 18 Nov: 3e limits, the fullest slot set found (outcome, cause, contributing, severity) in a non-aviation NTSB report read in extract; written after a failure, so Laura's sentences borrow the slots, never the past tense; word counts are Keel counts.

Wed 18 Nov: store, or Table 3's note; fix the use: SKELETON 3e opens with area (1) and its headline (Q105-043), so the failure answer heads the limits sentences, not 3e's first sentence; its second place is Table 3, never a repeat in prose.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e, the form for one ruled-out clause (not factors) beside Q109-032's fact; checked against NUMBERS 8u (no fall in any price in any set) and 8p's VT worthless row ($95,000, All paid); a fall still lowers what she can state before the move and shrinks her flexibility; never protected from crashes, never only two things can break the plan.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e, a contributing clause names the defence in seven words; Laura's sentence names a defence that holds (Treasuries she owns that pay each date), never one that failed; read at source.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e, precedent for naming what holds inside a failure sentence (the Treasuries and the payments' 0.5% margin since Tue 17 Nov evening, NUMBERS 2 checked); never borrow fortuitous, her protections are designed and owned.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e, the shortest form (one event, its mechanism, the outcome, 35 words), the size for a single-event set such as a US default; the fund-cost set needs two conditions together (NUMBERS 8u (e)), so not every sentence fits it.
Wed 18 Nov: store only, or a References fact if the NTSB form is cited; statute snippet read, not the whole section.

Wed 18 Nov: store; the counterfactual inside ICAO's contributing factor, run forwards for Laura (what would have to happen for a promise to break); judged after the event, so a source for the form only.

Wed 18 Nov: store, the evidence against one converged form (ICAO puts conclusions third); supports 3e taking the US order and leaving the evidence to NUMBERS and Table 2; a recommended practice states may adapt.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e and Table 3, a completeness test for the failure sentences beside Q109-028's caution; under the density cut the full sets live in NUMBERS 8u and Table 3, so prose names each promise's kinds of event and points there; Doc 9756 read only as quoted.

Wed 18 Nov: store only, beside Q4c and Q120-001: investigators number their probably at 66%; 3e borrows no hedge, and certain keeps the stated range (or the Treasuries) as its subject, never a figure.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e, a candidate aha clause: investigators dropped the single cause because complex accidents rarely have one, while Laura's failure sets are short because they rest on Treasuries she owns (NUMBERS 8u checked: a default in all three, a missed deposit in the payments' only, no price fall in any); short is not two, the payments' set has six events, so never only two things can break the plan; a pilots' position paper, not a test; test it cold before it takes a slot.
Wed 18 Nov: store; two words a 3e writer may borrow (causal breaks it alone, contributory makes it worse); one report read on its news page.

Wed 18 Nov: Table 3's note, a one-line definition of a watch from a real three-tier practice (a finding as to risk: not a factor now, could matter later); beside Q109-035's levels; Table 3's tiers are its own, so borrow the definition, never the TSB's tiers or its long lists.

Wed 18 Nov: Table 3, a condition-first shape for its Look closer or act when column (If ..., increasing the risk that ...); read at source; it runs cause to outcome, so keep Table 3's rows in one order and 3e's sentences in one order.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 12's contrast (accidents rarely have a single cause; Laura's sets are short), from the TSB; the card itself gives the aha to row 12, and Q109-016 holds the insurers' version.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e, a fixed cadence with fixed linking words (led to, increased the likelihood that) so a judge hears three parallel failure sentences, written to be understood by the cold reader; cause-first, the reverse of the NTSB's order, so pick one order for all three.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of Q109-009's two steps (define the failure, then the events), from a hospital guide; adds only that the order of finding causes need not be the order of writing them.

Wed 18 Nov: Table 3's Who column: a missed watch counts only where the plan gives the duty to Laura or her asset management team (Wharton's words, CASE_MAP 3e checked); rules for blame-free fixes, so a source for the column, never a new rule.

Wed 18 Nov: store, the finance version of the outcome-first form a judge knows; a source for the form only, since SKELETON 3e allows SVB once at most and spends it on no forced sale; 3e names events, never people.

Wed 18 Nov: store; fix the use: the FDIC's trigger and root cause are a sequence, while NUMBERS 8u (e) is two conditions needed together (fund costs past the 0.5% margin and waiting cash earning too little), so say and, not trigger then condition.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 20: the same 2023 bank failures in the inspectors' words; store only.
Wed 18 Nov: References, the bridge from accident reports to finance already in the investing literature, if 3e's form is cited; abstract read; about institutions, not wording.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e before Table 3: a warning before the steps; tested for compliance with product warnings, not comprehension, and not for outcome-before-cause order (the card's own verdict).

Wed 18 Nov: store, ANSI's four parts as a check on Table 3's five columns (signal, who, carry on while, look closer or act when, what it changes and never changes); the mapping is loose; ANSI Z535 itself not read.
Wed 18 Nov: store only; a third order (hazard, source, impacts) with no evaluation read; Table 3 already has its columns.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e, the tested case for naming the outcome specifically (a payment short or late on its 1 January, NUMBERS 8u checked) over a generic risk label; the odds are Keel arithmetic; the spread to products it did not cover is a caution, so each sentence names its own promise.
Wed 18 Nov: store, content beats prominence (6-10 points); order not isolated (row 31); supports what each sentence says over bold type.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e, give the three promise sentences equal standing so the weaker limit is not missed; web adverts, not a judge's careful read.

Wed 18 Nov: store, the counterweight to answer-first: a short cause-to-effect chain may read better for a mechanism (why a missed deposit breaks a payment but never a stated figure, Q109-031); abstract only; whole news articles.
Wed 18 Nov: a gap, not a finding, beside Q109-043: no test isolates outcome-first from cause-first; the blind two-version read on 27 Nov is the only test.
Wed 18 Nov: store; what high-impact writing included was not read, so never cite it as a test of bottom line first; abstract only.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of Q105-043 (the main point first, readable on one pass); adds only the name bottom line up front and active voice, from an Army rule, not investing literature.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e, evidence for claim 3: causal structure is recalled better than a collection; the assumptions keep the case's order and the limits take the causal form, as SKELETON 3e already splits them; abstract only, students not judges.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e and Table 3, the strongest tested case for tying each limit to the promise and figure it moves (NUMBERS 8u's rows) over a risks-first list; retail investors only, professionals showed no difference, so say so if cited; a revised working paper read in abstract and summary.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e, signal all five case areas as well as the failure sentences, or the unsignalled ones are lost; supports naming the case's five areas in order (Q37-002); abstract only.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e, numbering the five areas aids later recall; capture the authors at source before any citation (APA needs them); abstract only.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e, read at source: readers merge lists that sound alike and take the first bullet, so one clause must say IPS l.17's two reasons and the ways a promise breaks are different lists (Q109-033, CANON A34) and 8u's three verbs need a gloss at first use; a 16-person think-aloud on a broker form.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e and Table 3, put each failure sentence beside its Table 3 pointer and the two-lists clause beside the two reasons; read at source; same small sample as row 38.

Wed 18 Nov: for the 27 Nov writers, a checklist to test a 3e draft against; extends Q109-042 with the ruled-out clause, fixed linking words and the two-lists clause; the 200-word budget binds, so the areas that move no payment may share one sentence; adopt only after the blind two-version read (Q109-043).
